column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says hand and leaves the respondent unnamed; BSB uses arm and supplies Elisha.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says let us fall to the camp; BSB uses go over to the camp.
The Hebrew repeats the camp of Aram; BSB leaves Aram implicit in the second camp reference.
The Hebrew repeats sound for the chariotry, horses, and army; BSB combines them under one sound.
The Hebrew leaves the fleeing group unnamed; BSB supplies the Arameans.
The Hebrew coordinates entering the tent and eating and drinking as actions; BSB makes eating and drinking their purpose.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew first names a singular gatekeeper and explicitly mentions the absence of a human voice; BSB uses plural gatekeepers and says not a trace.
The Hebrew first uses a singular calling verb and then an active plural reporting verb; BSB makes the gatekeepers call and expresses the report passively.
The Hebrew uses a saying verb for their plan; BSB uses thinking.
The Hebrew does not name scouts and compares the horses with both those remaining and those already ended; BSB supplies scouts and rearranges the comparison around a doomed plight.
The Hebrew leaves the takers unnamed; BSB supplies scouts.
The Hebrew calls the returning men messengers; BSB uses scouts.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says hand and explicitly says that the king came down; BSB uses arm and leaves the descent implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the respondent unnamed; BSB supplies Elisha.
Close to the Hebrew.
